Distance and habit may seem like contradictory ideas, but in my dialectical way of thinking, they can both coexist and even complement each other. Let me explain how I see the connection.

Distance can mean physical space or even an emotional or psychological gap between people. When I cycle home from the hospital, the distance I cover symbolizes the time away from my daily routines, but also the need to return to those very routines. This physical distance can be a kind of liberation, away from the stresses of the night shift, but it can also create a need to reconnect with my daily rhythms, home, and family.

Habit, on the other hand, refers to the established routine that pulls us back to our daily lives. When I cycle through familiar streets at dawn, I follow routines that have become habits over the years. These habits are comforting and give structure to my life, even though I'm physically farther from my home at night. The distance I travel actually strengthens my habits because it makes me rely on them more to feel connected to my home and to my life beyond the night shift.
